title: University of Mauritius General Contact
description: The University of Mauritius is located at Réduit, 80837, Mauritius. The main telephone number is (230) 403 7400.

title: Admissions and Student Records Office (ASRO)
description: The Admissions and Student Records Office supports student enrolment, programme enquiries, admissions, fees, student progress and completion, student discipline and complaints. It is located at the Professor Sir Edouard Lim Fat Engineering Tower, University of Mauritius, Réduit. Telephone numbers include (230) 403 7872, (230) 403 7797 and (230) 403 7426. The admissions email is admission@uom.ac.mu.

title: University of Mauritius Examinations Office
description: The Examinations Office is located on the 1st Floor of the CPDL Building, University of Mauritius, Réduit. Contact numbers include (230) 403 7645, (230) 403 7635, (230) 403 7632 and (230) 403 7400 Ext. 2145.

title: University of Mauritius Library Contact
description: The University of Mauritius Library is located at the University of Mauritius, Réduit, Mauritius. The telephone number is (230) 403 7915 and the fax number is (230) 464 0905.

title: International Affairs Office - General Enquiries
description: International students can contact the University of Mauritius International Affairs Office for general enquiries using isao@uom.ac.mu. Contact numbers include +230 403 7440 and +230 5902 5055.

title: International Applicants - Application Enquiries
description: International applicants who have already applied and need information about their application can use studyatuom@uom.ac.mu. Contact numbers include +230 403 1135, +230 403 7825, +230 403 1310 and +230 5532 5984.

title: University of Mauritius Students' Union
description: The Students' Union is the official organisation representing students at the University of Mauritius. It promotes student welfare and supports social, cultural and educational activities, clubs and societies. The office is at the Student Centre, University of Mauritius, Réduit.

title: University of Mauritius Student Counselling
description: The University of Mauritius provides counselling support for students experiencing personal, academic or other difficulties that may affect their studies. Students may be referred through the Admissions and Student Records Office to appropriate professionals when required.

title: University of Mauritius First Aid Services
description: The University of Mauritius provides First Aid services for students and staff. Students who require medical assistance on campus can use the University's First Aid facilities.

title: University of Mauritius Student Welfare and Financial Assistance
description: The University of Mauritius provides student welfare support and financial assistance schemes for eligible students. Students should consult the official financial assistance information for current eligibility requirements, supporting documents and deadlines.

title: Faculty of Agriculture
description: The Faculty of Agriculture includes the Department of Agricultural Production & Systems and the Department of Agricultural & Food Science.

title: Faculty of Engineering
description: The Faculty of Engineering includes the Department of Chemical and Environmental Engineering, Department of Civil Engineering, Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Department of Applied Sustainability and Enterprise Development, and Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering.

title: Faculty of Information, Communication and Digital Technologies
description: The Faculty of Information, Communication and Digital Technologies includes the Department of Digital Technologies, Department of Information and Communication Technologies, and Department of Software and Information Systems.

title: Department of Information and Communication Technologies
description: The Department of Information and Communication Technologies is part of the Faculty of Information, Communication and Digital Technologies and offers programmes including BSc (Hons) Computer Science and BSc (Hons) Cyber Security.

title: Department of Software and Information Systems
description: The Department of Software and Information Systems is part of the Faculty of Information, Communication and Digital Technologies. Its areas include business systems, enterprise applications, software development, information management, knowledge management, big data, information systems, data science and artificial intelligence.

title: Faculty of Law and Management
description: The Faculty of Law and Management includes the Department of Finance & Accounting, Department of Law and Department of Management.

title: Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences
description: The Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences includes the Department of Medicine and Department of Health Sciences. The faculty also hosts an Ayurveda Chair.

title: Faculty of Science
description: The Faculty of Science includes the Department of Biological Sciences and Ocean Studies, Department of Chemistry, Department of Mathematics and Department of Physics.

title: Faculty of Social Sciences and Humanities
description: The Faculty of Social Sciences and Humanities includes the Department of Economics and Statistics, Department of English Studies, Department of French Studies, Department of History and Political Science, and Department of Social Studies.

title: University of Mauritius Regulations 2026/2027
description: The University of Mauritius publishes regulations covering admissions, programme structure, registration, assessment, examinations, academic integrity, final year projects, fees, welfare and other student matters. The 2026/2027 regulations are marked as under review and may be subject to change.

title: Admission Requirements
description: Applicants must follow the University's prescribed application procedure and satisfy both the University's general entry requirements and the specific entry requirements of the programme for which they apply.

title: Programme Structure and Credit System
description: University regulations define programme structure, module types, credits, contact hours, programme duration, industrial or professional placements and other programme requirements. Students should also consult their programme catalogue for programme-specific requirements.

title: Module Registration and Changes
description: University regulations cover module registration, module changes, module withdrawal, late module registration, deregistration and module exemptions. Students must follow the applicable procedures and deadlines.

title: Attendance Requirements
description: Students are expected to attend the lectures, tutorials and other forms of instruction prescribed by their programme. Attendance may be monitored and students should check the specific attendance requirements applicable to their programme and modules.

title: Student Conduct and Discipline
description: Students are expected to conduct themselves in a manner consistent with the objectives and well-being of the University as an academic community. Breaches of University discipline may result in disciplinary action under the University's Code of Discipline.

title: Assessment Methods
description: Student assessment may include written examinations, continuous assessment, laboratory work, seminars, assignments and class tests. The exact weighting and assessment structure should be checked in the relevant module specification or programme documentation.

title: GPA, CPA and Academic Progress
description: The University uses measures including Grade Point Average and Cumulative Point Average in academic assessment and progression. Students should consult the regulations and their programme structure for the progression requirements that apply to their cohort.

title: Retakes, Resits and Reassessment
description: University regulations include provisions for retake modules, resit examinations, special retake examinations, reassessment and re-submission of dissertations in applicable circumstances.

title: Absence from an Examination Due to Illness
description: Students who miss an examination because of ill health must follow the University's medical absence procedure and submit the required valid medical certificate within the prescribed period. Students should consult the current examination regulations for the exact conditions and deadlines.

title: Examination Conduct and Unauthorised Devices
description: Students must comply with examination instructions and invigilator directions. Use of unauthorised devices during an examination may constitute an examination irregularity and may lead to disciplinary procedures.

title: Examination Irregularities and Appeals
description: Suspected examination irregularities may be referred through the University's disciplinary procedure. The regulations also provide procedures relating to notification, disciplinary decisions and appeals.

title: Plagiarism
description: Plagiarism includes presenting another person's work, ideas or material as one's own without appropriate acknowledgement. This can include copying, insufficient citation, unacknowledged paraphrasing or use of online material without proper attribution.

title: Fabrication and Falsification
description: Fabrication or falsification of results, data or documents is treated as an academic integrity offence under University regulations.

title: Use of Artificial Intelligence in Academic Work
description: The University regulations emphasise responsible and ethical use of Artificial Intelligence. AI use must be appropriately attributed or referenced where required, and it must not compromise academic integrity or authorship.

title: Final Year Project and Dissertation Regulations
description: Final year projects and dissertations are governed by University requirements covering project allocation, supervision, project work, referencing, assessment, submission, declaration forms, progress records and other applicable procedures.

title: Turnitin and Final Year Project Submission
description: Final year project and dissertation submissions must comply with the University's academic integrity and submission requirements, including applicable Turnitin procedures.

title: Final Year Project Assessment
description: Final year projects and dissertations are assessed according to the University's prescribed procedures. Depending on programme requirements, assessment may include the written dissertation, viva-voce, poster presentation or other assessment components.

title: University Fees and Charges
description: University regulations cover applicable tuition and general fees as well as other charges such as registration, reassessment, re-registration, review, transcript, certificate and graduation-related fees. Students should check current official information because fees may be reviewed.

title: Students with Disabilities
description: University regulations include provisions concerning students with disabilities, including admission, facilities, applicable regulations and certification requirements.

title: Student Academic Progress and Complaints
description: The University has provisions relating to student academic progress and complaints, including the role and procedures of the relevant University committee.
